blocks.text: This chapter explores the key computational structures, lists, stacks, queues, trees and graphs, which are fundamental in programming: their properties, operations and efficient implementation, how to choose the right structure for a problem, and their use in real-world scenarios.
In daily life we organize data: contacts on a phone, a to-do list, plates stacked in a kitchen. Computers also need to organize and manage data, and computational structures help them do it.
